Max Sturtevant (Max Wellcopy) Content Playbook

Scraped 2026-11-25: last 90 days in detail plus all-time best. Numbers are from public pages; his hours are estimates. Copy his method, not his words. Everything in Juan's version uses Juan's voice and topics.

1. The picture in one paragraph

Max runs an email and SMS agency (Well Copy, ~90 people, 100+ brands on retainer). He posts about 50 times a week across five platforms. Most of it is cheap: a screenshot of an email plus a verdict ("this is a 0/10 order confirmation"). The raw material is free — his and his clients' inboxes fill with emails every day. A few posts a week are long and personal (life lessons, agency honesty, grind stories); those win reach and comments. The screenshot posts win saves. Nearly every post carries proof ("$500M+ for clients"). Every profile points to one paid community (Skool, $247/mo, ~438 members). Brands that follow him for 6–24 months book a call with the agency. It works because volume keeps his name in front of the same people daily, the formats repeat so each post is quick, and a scheduler, an auto-repost tool and keyword auto-DMs do the follow-up — he hardly ever replies by hand.

- Post on 84 of 89 days; weekends added June. Median likes fell ~100 → ~60 as volume rose.
- Hooks: vague tease over carousel ("Almost nobody is doing this 👀"), steal + number, life confession, contrarian, list with colon, client result, famous name.
- Caption-only posts ~8 words over 5–6 page PDF. Long posts 150–540 words + one photo, 1–2 sentences per line, punchline close. Slang, mild swearing, hashtags 4/300.
- Replies to 0 of 293 normal comments; on lead magnets 144 "[Name] sent!" in two bursts — delivery, not conversation.
- Commenters: ~half email freelancers, ~quarter founders. His trade, not buyers.

8. What not to copy

  1. Volume watered down LinkedIn (median likes ~100 → ~60).
  2. Zero replies — works at 138K followers, not when starting small.
  3. His audience is his trade, not buyers. Juan's must be founders/heads of growth.
  4. Off-niche virality is worthless (274K TikTok, no buyers).
  5. Unlabelled sponsored posts — disclosure risk.
  6. Generic hot takes get comments, not expertise.
  7. Own case studies are his worst YouTube format; famous brands beat "my client".
  8. Gen-Z slang and swearing are his voice, not Juan's.
  9. Weekend daily posting added count, not results (except Sunday on X).

Hard filters on every piece: no Mars Men numbers, tests or implementations; no ASTEROI client names or numbers; no men's-health/hormone/testosterone/men's-supplement brands in rankings or studies (non-compete §5.2, confidentiality §5.6); no Meta ads/creative/ad-spend advice (Raheel's area).

Raw material engine: (1) swipe inbox + screenshot folder — subscribe to 50–100 DTC brands outside men's health, buy small things to see checkouts, send everything via Telegram to life/raw/inbox/; (2) the vault — 37 ASTEROI articles, frameworks, LinkedIn archive drafts; (3) public brand data for studies; (4) own tests on a personal/demo site.

OPEN QUESTIONS (Juan decides): - What does the funnel sell? Paid community, course, audits, ASTEROI, or nothing yet? - Name ASTEROI publicly? (Phase 1 says no; client roster firewalled.) - Bio says "Head of eCommerce at Mars Men"? Strongest credential, but every post reflects on Mars Men. - Hire an editor/thumbnail designer? - Paid tool partnerships? (Risk: reveals Mars Men's tools; disclosure.) - First free guide behind a keyword? - Weekend posting? (Evidence: only Sunday on X is worth it.) - Where to film; green screen? - Rewrite content-strategy page (currently X 3–5/wk, LinkedIn 1–2/wk)?
